entities.summary:
The Meditations of Marcus Aurelius are a timeless collection of philosophical thoughts and reflections written by the Roman Emperor Marcus Aurelius (121–180 CE). Born in Rome, Italy, and ruling as Emperor from 161 to 180 CE, Aurelius is known for his wisdom, justice, and military prowess. In these meditations, he grapples with fundamental questions about human existence, the nature of reality, and the meaning of life. Written around 170–180 CE, the Meditations are a culmination of his personal experiences as a ruler, philosopher, and individual who sought to live in harmony with himself and the world around him.

This work has had a profound impact on Western philosophy, influencing thinkers such as Immanuel Kant, Jean-Jacques Rousseau, and Friedrich Nietzsche. Its value lies not only in its insight into human psychology but also in its ability to provide guidance for personal growth, leadership, and spiritual development. The Meditations continue to be studied and cherished by scholars, philosophers, and individuals around the world, offering a profound exploration of the human condition.
